newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM earnings plunge, chief executive to resign.
newsitem.headline: KLM earnings plunge, chief executive to resign.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said Wednesday its profits fell sharply in its last fiscal year as costs rose faster than revenues and the bottom line was hit by a hefty restructuring charge aimed at boosting future earnings.

KLM also unexpectedly announced its president and chief executive Pieter Bouw would step down in August after six years at the helm to allow someone else to oversee a crucial recovery plan for the airline.
The company said its net profit for the year ended March 31 fell to 236 million guilders ($125.2 million) from 547 million ($290 million).

This included a pre-tax provision of 290 million guilders ($153.8 million) for the Focus 2000 restructuring programme, which aims to boost operating profits by 1.5 billion guilders ($795 million) over three years.

But KLM said this was not the only factor behind the steep drop in earnings, noting that operating costs had risen by 13 percent while operating revenues rose only 8.6 percent -- thus continuing a trend which had already started in the previous fiscal year.
Consequently, operating profit, before the restructuring provision, fell to 89 million guilders ($47.2 million) from 453 million ($240.3 million).
"This is a clear proof of the necessity for the new and substantial transformation process that has been initiated under the name Focus 2000," it said.
KLM said Bouw, 55, would resign as CEO at the annual meeting Aug. 5 and that the company's supervisory board planned to appoint chief operating officer Leo van Wijk, 50, to succeed him.

KLM said it regretted Bouw's decision but that after more than six years in charge of KLM, and at the dawn of a major restructuring programme, Bouw felt the time was ripe for a transfer of leadership.

The slide in KLM's earnings came despite a higher contribution from its U.S. associate, Northwest Airlines Corp., of 442 million guilders ($234.5 million) vs. 258 million ($136.9 million) in the prior year.
This was mainly derived from the sale and revaluation of various types of NWA shares, but the fourth quarter also brought 59 million guilders ($31.3 million) in operational profits from Northwest.
